Upgrading from dsh 0.1 first."},{"id":"p15s1","text":"## Getting it running"},{"id":"p16s1","text":"### 1. Install Bridle on the Mac"},{"id":"p17s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p18s1","text":"Needs Node 22+ and git — the script installs neither; it stops and tells you
what is missing — and d"},{"id":"p18s2","text":"sh 0.2, which it checks for and warns about. Everything it installs lives in `~/.rowel`, plus one sy"},{"id":"p18s3","text":"mlink onto
your PATH (and npm's usual cache). It is 144 lines, over a third of them
comments, if you"},{"id":"p18s4","text":" would rather read it before running it."},{"id":"p19s1","text":"### 2. Pair"},{"id":"p20s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p21s1","text":"It starts Bridle if none is running, prints a QR code, and stays running. In
the app, tap *Connect a"},{"id":"p21s2","text":" Mac*, then *I've run it — scan the code*. With Bridle
already running (a service, or dsh's plugin),"},{"id":"p21s3","text":" it just prints a fresh code.
`--code` does the same, for typing instead of scanning."},{"id":"p22s1","text":"**If dsh is already running** — started by hand, or kept up by a login item —
Bridle cannot sign in "},{"id":"p22s2","text":"to it from outside: dsh 0.2 hands its sign-in token only
to its own plugins. Run Bridle inside it in"},{"id":"p22s3","text":"stead, then restart dsh:"},{"id":"p23s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p24s1","text":"`bridle status` says which of the two you have, and `bridle doctor` says what
to do when it is neith"},{"id":"p24s2","text":"er. Left to itself, with no dsh running, Bridle starts one
and signs in with the token it prints."},{"id":"p25s1","text":"Over SSH, where a terminal may not draw a QR code, add `--link` to print the raw
pairing link. When "},{"id":"p25s2","text":"the camera is not an option, `bridle pair --code` prints an
8-character code to type instead and wai"},{"id":"p25s3","text":"ts: the Mac then shows the phone's key
and asks you to accept it, and you check it against the key t"},{"id":"p25s4","text":"he phone shows.
SECURITY.md says why that step exists."},{"id":"p26s1","text":"### 3. Keep it running"},{"id":"p27s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"Starts after login and survives closing the terminal. `bridle service uninstall`
takes it back off."},{"id":"p29s1","text":"## The `bridle` command"},{"id":"p30s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p31s1","text":"Useful flags on `bridle` itself:"},{"id":"p32s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p33s1","text":"State lives in `~/.rowel/bridle.json`, mode `0600`, and it holds this machine's
private key. `ROWEL_"},{"id":"p33s2","text":"`~/.rowel/bridle.json`, mode `0600`, and it holds this machine's
private key. `ROWEL_HOME` moves it."},{"id":"p34s1","text":"## Two harnesses on one Mac"},{"id":"p35s1","text":"One Bridle serves one dsh. Left to itself it probes the usual ports (3080–3083,
8080, 8791) and stay"},{"id":"p35s2","text":"s with whichever dsh answered last time — fine with one
harness, a coin toss with two. `--dsh` ends "},{"id":"p35s3","text":"ver dsh answered last time — fine with one
harness, a coin toss with two. `--dsh` ends the guessing:"},{"id":"p36s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p37s1","text":"If nothing answers there, Bridle starts a harness on that exact port — the
startup line says `(start"},{"id":"p37s2","text":"ed by bridle)` when it did. `--no-auto-start` makes it
refuse instead."},{"id":"p38s1","text":"[该节后续省略]"},{"id":"p39s1","text":"## What it is protecting, and what it is not"},{"id":"p40s1","text":"The relay switches sealed frames between two sockets by circuit number. It has no
key material and c"},{"id":"p40s2","text":"annot open them, which is a property of the shape rather than a
promise about anyone's conduct — an "},{"id":"p40s3","text":"end-to-end test taps the phone's traffic
through the relay and fails if a method name, a session id,"},{"id":"p40s4","text":" the machine's name or
a conversation title ever appears in it. (The relay does learn the machine's
"},{"id":"p40s5","text":"display name from Bridle's own registration; SECURITY.md lists everything it
learns.) Both
implement"},{"id":"p40s6","text":"ations of the tunnel use only their platform's own primitives, Node's
`node:crypto` and Swift's `Cry"},{"id":"p40s7","text":"ptoKit`. There is no third-party cryptography
dependency in the tree."},{"id":"p41s1","text":"**The part people underestimate:** dsh asks a browser for nothing more than the
token it printed, an"},{"id":"p41s2","text":"d Bridle holds that sign-in, so a paired phone has the same
authority over that Mac as its own termi"},{"id":"p41s3","text":"nal — it can
run commands and read and write files. `bridle revoke` is the only way to take
that bac"},{"id":"p41s4","text":"k. Nothing in the app is a smaller permission than that; the app just
draws fewer buttons."},{"id":"p42s1","text":"SECURITY.md is the full threat model, including what the relay
does learn, what an unlocked phone me"},{"id":"p42s2","text":"ans, and the known weaknesses. It is worth
reading before you pair anything you care about."}],"truncated":true}
